chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q3 SCOTUS Comparison (4 points) — Set 2: Shaw v. Reno
chunks.content: AP Government FRQ 3, SCOTUS Comparison, 4 points, comparing the required case Shaw v. Reno with a non-required case in the prompt. A [1] identify the common constitutional clause/provision at the basis of both decisions. B [2] explain how the facts of the two cases led to different (or similar) holdings (two points). C [1] explain how the holding relates to a course concept or affects policy/politics. Same 1-2-1 point structure as Set 1. Common failure: wrong shared clause in A; facts described without linking to the holdings (B); describing rather than explaining the concept in C.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q3 Set 2 exemplar — Sample 3A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 2) scored 4/4 (A 1, B 2, C 1). Identified the shared clause, explained how the two cases' facts produced their holdings (both B points), and explained the holding's relationship to a course concept. Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q3 Set 2 exemplar — Sample 3B, 2/4
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 2) scored 2/4 — typically earned A (shared clause) and one of the two B points, losing the second B point and C. Illustrates a response that identifies the clause and part of the comparison but cannot complete the facts-to-holdings link or apply the concept.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q3 Set 2 exemplar — Sample 3C, 1/4
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 2) scored 1/4 — earned only one point (typically A). Lost both B points (no valid facts-to-holdings comparison) and C. Illustrates a response confined to naming the shared clause.
